label: sequence started with j: late original steps and <DEL>
explanation: Fires when the first original token is j, from step 3 of the original phase through the <DEL> step, whatever token is input at those steps. It is silent at steps 0-2 and almost entirely silent in the copy phase, including at the step that outputs the leading j. On dev, 93% of activation mass comes from j-first sequences, and the predicate has precision 0.99. Activation rises over the first few steps after t=3 (around 0.2 of max at t=3, near max at t=4-6) and then eases off toward <DEL>. The strongest activations are in sequences beginning j j; j d is next. Missed activations (about 6.7% of mass) are weak firings at late original steps when j is the second original token instead of the first. Adding those raises recall but drops precision to 0.65.

issues: Core claims check out. Copy phase is silent (t > L: precision 0.00006, mass 0.04%). Steps 0-2 are silent. Activation ramps from t=3 (0.10 of mass) to a peak at t=4-6 and fades by t=9. 93% of mass comes from j-first sequences. Test precision is 0.99 and mass recall 0.936.
Count recall is only 0.73: 27% of active steps (27,335 on test) are missed. Most are low-quartile firings (quartile coverage 0.16 and 0.76), so they fall outside the label.

The secondary class is systematic, not noise. When j is the second original token (and not the first), the feature fires weakly at mid-original steps. Rule: (first_tok != j) & (orig(1) == j) & (t <= L), precision 0.30, recall 0.21. Restricted to t=5..6 its precision is 0.58-0.59. It never fires at t=3, so this is a lagged version of the j-first response. The explanation says adding this class drops precision to 0.65; that only holds for the broad version. Restricting it to t in 5..7 and t < L keeps the combined precision at 0.90.

Systematic false-positive class: j-first sequences with j as the third token (j ? j) are always inactive at t=3. Rule: (first_tok==j)&(t==3)&(orig(2)==j), precision 0.0. This covers most of the 737 false positives on test. The explanation does not mention it.
The remaining misses with no j in the first two positions are scattered and weak (precision 0.003, 0.4% of mass). That part is acceptable noise.
Better predicate: test F1 0.887 versus 0.840, with mass recall 0.982 and precision 0.90.
skeptic.revised_label: j as first original token: original steps 3 through <DEL> (silent at t=3 when the third token is also j); weaker, delayed firing at steps 5-7 when j is the second token
